articles.summary: The National Testing Agency has released the provisional answer keys for 84 subjects of the UGC-NET 2026 examinations. Candidates can submit challenges to the keys until August 18 by paying a processing fee of 200 rupees per questioned item.

articles.summary: Former competitive dancers Jack Anderson and Charlotte Mclean, alongside piper Malin Lewis, present an anarchic dance-theatre performance at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe. The trio deconstructs and mocks their traditional Scottish and Irish dance backgrounds, ultimately reclaiming their artistic inheritance through a contemporary lens.

articles.summary: Iraqi judicial authorities seized over 20 million dollars in cash, 60 kilograms of gold, and multiple vehicles linked to a senior oil ministry official as part of an ongoing corruption investigation. The operation involves coordinated efforts between central and regional courts to recover assets lost through financial irregularities.

articles.title: Russian Anti-War Protesters in Japan Continue Demonstrations
articles.summary: Russian expatriates living in Japan are persisting with their anti-war demonstrations despite years of conflict and uncertainty. articles.title: Egypt Stance on Ethiopian Dam Projects

articles.summary: The Egyptian National Railways Authority has announced an ongoing application process for lecturer and assistant professor positions specializing in power mechanical engineering. articles.summary: Sources report that approximately 2,000 applications regarding exotic animals are currently pending before the Chief Wildlife Warden in Tamil Nadu, who serves as the final authority for state approvals. articles.summary: Political leaders including Fadnavis and Pawar commemorated the death anniversary of former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee. articles.summary: Claressa Shields secured a sixth-round technical knockout victory against Kaye Scott in Atlanta. The win allowed Shields to successfully reclaim her WBC and WBA middleweight championship titles.

articles.summary: Celebrations marking Indian Independence Day in the New York Tri-State area concluded with a notable achievement on Saturday. A new Guinness World Record for the largest flagpole number was officially set during an event held at the Veterans Memorial Park in Parsippany, New Jersey.

articles.summary: A parliamentary standing committee has recommended establishing a task force to address 38 vacant positions within DIPAM. articles.title: Crews tackle warehouse blaze in early hours
articles.summary: A neighbouring county fire service also receives calls from concerned residents as smoke spreads.

articles.title: Gen Z Women and Period Education

articles.title: Alaskan Bearcam Livestream Popularity
articles.summary: A livestream featuring brown bears catching and eating salmon at Brooks Falls in Alaska's Katmai National Park has drawn millions of views ahead of Fat Bear Week. The popular wildlife broadcast recorded millions of streams, reflecting a substantial increase in online viewership compared to previous years for the natural spectacle.

articles.title: AI Holiday Photo Scams Target Bank Accounts
articles.summary: Fraudsters are utilizing artificial intelligence and public holiday photos shared on social media platforms like Instagram and Facebook to target travelers. By analyzing location backgrounds, criminals send fraudulent text messages claiming bank cards have been compromised during the trip, attempting to trick victims into revealing sensitive financial details and personal information.

articles.title: Prix Jacques le Marois Field Set
articles.summary: Horse racing contenders Precise, More Thunder, and Zeus Olympios are scheduled to compete in the upcoming Prix Jacques Le Marois. The prominent racing event will be broadcast live on Sky Sports Racing, drawing attention from racing enthusiasts following the confirmation of the competing lineup for the fixture.

articles.title: Hong Kong Defends Talent Scheme
articles.summary: Hong Kong's immigration chief has dismissed claims that world-class snooker players are utilizing local talent schemes solely to minimize tax liabilities. Director of Immigration Benson Kwok Joon-fung emphasized that the city's robust public safety, efficient transportation infrastructure, and quality education system are the primary attractions for global professionals relocating there.

articles.title: Hurricane Lala Brings Heavy Rain
articles.summary: Hurricane Lala, a Category 1 storm, has brought heavy rainfall and strong winds to Hawaii, prompting the declaration of a state of emergency. Forecasters warn the hurricane could dump up to 25 inches of rain, potentially causing life-threatening flooding and severe mudslides across vulnerable communities throughout the islands.

articles.title: Vietnam Airlines Boeing 787 returns to Munich
articles.summary: A Vietnam Airlines Boeing 787 flight returned to Munich shortly after takeoff due to a technical issue. Flight tracking data and airport reports indicated the aircraft experienced problems, prompting the crew to follow standard safety procedures and return to the departure airport. All passengers and crew members were reported safe, and authorities are inspecting the aircraft.

articles.title: Highlights from Test Match Action
articles.summary: Day four of the first Test match between Australia and Bangladesh featured notable moments, including Litton Das being caught out of position behind the stumps and Mehidy Hasan Miraz facing a difficult dismissal in front of the wicket. The ongoing contest delivered several dramatic passages of play for cricket fans.

articles.title: Belfast Hosts First Fleadh Festival
articles.summary: Organisers and participants have praised the transformational impact of Belfast hosting its first Fleadh cultural festival. The event brought significant cultural and community engagement to the city throughout its duration.

articles.title: Former Bengal Minister Asish Banerjee Found Dead
articles.summary: Asish Banerjee, a former West Bengal minister and Trinamool Congress leader, was found dead inside a party office. A note was recovered claiming he had no involvement in corruption and alleging attempts to damage his reputation. His body has been transferred for an autopsy as police investigate the incident.

articles.title: US Trade Policy Shifts Will Primarily Impact Hong Kong Psychologically
articles.summary: Hong Kong's Financial Secretary Paul Chan stated that upcoming shifts in US trade policies and interest rates will primarily have a psychological impact on the local economy. Chan expressed optimism that economic growth momentum will persist into the second half of the year, following the government's recent upward revision of its full-year growth forecast.

articles.title: Claressa Shields Defeats Kaye Scott
articles.summary: American multi-division world champion Claressa Shields defeated Australia's Kaye Scott in the sixth round at the State Farm Arena in Atlanta, claiming the WBA and WBC middleweight titles. Following the bout, Shields identified Lauren Price as her preferred next opponent.

articles.title: Ireland's Growing Commercial Vineyards
articles.summary: Despite traditionally being known for other beverages, Ireland's commercial wine industry is seeing an increase in land being planted with vineyards, marking a gradual expansion of small-scale domestic wine production in the country.

articles.title: Meta Increases Censorship of Political and Protest Content
articles.summary: Meta has blocked numerous Instagram posts in India from political party accounts, representatives, and ordinary protesters. Reports indicate that the platform is restricting certain political content even when removal is not legally mandated.

articles.title: Vietnam Airlines Flight Returns to Munich
articles.summary: A Vietnam Airlines Boeing 787 bound for Hanoi returned to Munich Airport after encountering a technical issue during takeoff. The aircraft circled to burn fuel before landing, where it remained stranded on the runway, causing temporary air traffic rerouting and runway closure. The airline confirmed that all passengers and crew members are safe.

articles.title: Islam Makhachev Retains UFC Welterweight Title
articles.summary: Islam Makhachev secured a unanimous decision victory over Ian Machado Garry in the main event of UFC 330 in Philadelphia to retain his welterweight title. The win marks Makhachev's 17th consecutive victory in the promotion, setting a new promotional record through a combination of effective wrestling and striking.

articles.title: Colombian President Requests US Tariff Suspension After Earthquake
articles.summary: Following a deadly earthquake that killed at least 300 people and devastated the cities of Cali and Pereira, Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella has formally asked United States President Donald Trump to suspend tariffs on the South American nation. The country is currently managing extensive recovery efforts and widespread infrastructure damage.

articles.title: NATO Fighter Jet Shoots Down Drone Over Romania
articles.summary: The Romanian Ministry of Defense announced that a Spanish pilot flying an F-18 fighter jet on a NATO air policing mission shot down a drone that had violated Romanian airspace. The interception was executed as part of routine alliance defense measures in the region.

articles.title: Saudi Actor Mohammed Al-Doukhi Discusses Career
articles.summary: In an interview with Asharq Al-Awsat, Saudi actor and producer Mohammed Al-Doukhi reflected on his acting career. He discussed his transition across various genres, moving from comedy to drama, action, and crime, while focusing on complex character development rather than traditional heroic tropes.

articles.title: African Diplomacy in Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: African governments have maintained a low public profile during the ongoing crisis in the Strait of Hormuz. Despite the lack of prominent international statements, diplomatic engagement regarding the situation is actively taking place behind the scenes.

articles.title: Congress Leader P. Chidambaram Responds to Prime Minister
articles.summary: Senior Congress leader P. Chidambaram responded to the Prime Minister's recent warnings about systemic internal threats, adopting the critical label in his remarks. The exchange follows government statements regarding individuals allegedly entrenched within national institutions.

articles.title: Egypt Weather Forecast: High Heat and Humidity
articles.summary: The Egyptian Meteorological Authority predicts hot and humid weather conditions across most regions at the beginning of the week. Temperatures are expected to feel particularly high, reaching approximately 38 degrees Celsius in Cairo, with morning conditions remaining warm and humid throughout the area.

articles.title: Bangladesh Secures Historic Test Victory in Australia
articles.summary: Bangladesh defeated Australia by nine wickets in Darwin to secure their first-ever Test match victory on Australian soil. Despite a century from Cameron Green, Australia was bowled out for 284 in their second innings. Bangladesh successfully chased the 57-run target, achieving a historic milestone in Test cricket history.

articles.title: Spain Floods Kill Two
articles.summary: Torrential rain triggered a deadly flood and landslide in rural northwestern Spain, resulting in the deaths of two women and injuring two babies, local authorities reported. The severe weather event follows weeks of persistent heatwaves and destructive wildfires across the country.

articles.title: Bafta-Winning Documentary Airs on Television
articles.summary: A Bafta-winning documentary following the life of Mir Hussein in Afghanistan over a 25-year period is scheduled for television broadcast. The program highlights the long-term impact of conflict through individual experiences, offering viewers an in-depth look at ongoing developments in the region.

articles.title: Supporting Berlin Pride Attack Victims
articles.summary: Following terrorist incidents, public attention typically centers on perpetrators rather than the individuals affected. This report examines the support available to victims of the Berlin Pride attack, exploring what assistance they can expect and how they navigate their ongoing recovery process.

articles.title: UK Drones Used in Russia and Phone Thefts
articles.summary: Sunday newspaper reports indicate that Ukraine has utilized British-manufactured drones in military strikes against Russia. Additionally, domestic headlines highlight a rising crime rate in the UK, with an estimated 230 mobile phones stolen daily across the country.

articles.title: New Shinkansen Model Delivered
articles.summary: A new shinkansen bullet train model has been delivered to Taiwan. Designated as the N700ST and based on the latest design from JR Central, the new high-speed train is engineered to produce less noise and vibration while consuming lower amounts of electricity compared to previous generations of rolling stock.

articles.title: Sculptor Chandrashekhar Shilpi Passes Away
articles.summary: Renowned sculptor Chandrashekhar Shilpi has passed away. He was widely recognized for his dedication to preserving the sculptural heritage of Kalyana Karnataka through intricate and traditional wood and stone carvings.

articles.title: Lani Pallister Defeats Katie Ledecky
articles.summary: Australian swimmer Lani Pallister secured victory in the 800-meter freestyle at the Pan Pacific Championships in Irvine, California, setting a new championship record of 8:06.10. The result ended the United States competitor Katie Ledecky's long-standing winning streak of 13 international gold medals in the event.

articles.title: The Evolution of the Two-Day Weekend
articles.summary: Marking a century since Henry Ford popularized the two-day weekend, this article explores the history of designated rest days. It contrasts the modern weekend model with historical experiments, such as the Soviet Union's abolished staggered calendar, while discussing contemporary shifts toward hybrid work arrangements.

articles.title: UK Faces Renewed Cost of Living Squeeze
articles.summary: British households are facing a renewed cost of living crisis as official figures are expected to show that soaring energy bills pushed inflation close to three percent in July. Spillovers from global energy markets continue to drive up gas and electricity prices, creating mounting economic pressures for the government.

articles.title: Alaves Beats Getafe in La Liga Opener
articles.summary: Deportivo Alaves commenced their new Spanish La Liga football season with a strong victory, defeating Getafe with three goals to nil in their opening match on Saturday.

articles.title: Bayern Munich Wins Women's Super Cup
articles.summary: Bayern Munich secured the German Women's Super Cup title after defeating VfL Wolfsburg. This victory marks the third consecutive time the team has claimed the championship trophy.

articles.title: Xbox Marks 25 Years in Gaming Industry
articles.summary: Microsoft entered the console gaming market in November 2001 with the release of the original Xbox, challenging established Japanese competitors like Sony and Nintendo. Although it did not outsell the PlayStation 2 commercially, the console introduced broadband multiplayer and shaped the future of online gaming infrastructure.

articles.title: Meet Ajisai, a Visually Impaired Rescue
articles.summary: Ajisai is a rescue animal with a visual impairment who may initially feel nervous around unfamiliar people. Despite her cautious nature, she gradually warms up and affectionate behavior helps her form lasting bonds with new caretakers.

articles.title: Léon Marchand Wins European Title
articles.summary: French swimmer Léon Marchand secured his first continental title by winning the 200m butterfly final at the European Championships in Paris. During the same event, compatriot Mary-Ambre Moluh set a new European record to claim gold in the 100m backstroke final.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Targets Drug Menace
articles.summary: Governments continue to face challenges in curbing drug distribution networks. In Tamil Nadu, authorities are deploying a specialized Anti-Narcotics Task Force to address the rising availability of substances and early youth addiction across the state.

articles.title: Indonesian Earthquake Survivors Recount Ordeal
articles.summary: At least 48 people were killed and dozens injured after a powerful 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck near Indonesia's Flores Island. Survivors recounted chaotic scenes as buildings collapsed, forcing patients and families to flee hospitals and homes for safety during the early morning tremor.

articles.title: Japanese Defense Minister Visits Australia
articles.summary: Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi is scheduled to visit Canberra to meet with Australian counterpart Richard Marles. The discussions will primarily focus on Australia's acquisition of Japanese Mogami-class frigates and bilateral security cooperation, following recent diplomatic discussions.

articles.title: Drones Target Moscow and Kyiv
articles.summary: The Moscow region was targeted by a large-scale overnight drone assault involving hundreds of devices, injuring three people, according to local officials. Simultaneously, Russian forces launched missile attacks against Kyiv, triggering fires in multiple districts of the Ukrainian capital.

articles.title: Egypt Starts Entrance Exams for STEM High Schools
articles.summary: The Egyptian Ministry of Education has scheduled the start of electronic entrance exams for students applying to STEM high schools for the upcoming academic year. Eligible candidates include those who have successfully completed their preparatory school education, as announced by official educational authorities.

articles.title: Poll Shows Strong Support for Traffic Enforcement in Egypt
articles.summary: An opinion poll conducted by Youm7 indicates that 91 percent of participating readers support intensifying traffic campaigns to crack down on motorists who violate road safety rules and regulations. The survey reflects public sentiment regarding the need for stricter traffic law enforcement.

articles.title: Arrest After Incident at Surrey Hotel
articles.summary: A man in his twenties remains in police custody following an alleged stabbing incident at the Stanwell Hotel in Surrey. Officers were called to the scene, and the suspect is currently being held on suspicion of attempted murder while investigations continue.

articles.title: Minister Outlines Development Goals
articles.summary: A government minister has urged local officials to work toward the objectives established for the 'Swarna Kadapa 2047' initiative. The announcement included details regarding substantial financial allocations directed toward municipal administration, water resources, and tourism development.

articles.title: Hong Kong Heatwave Persists
articles.summary: Scorching weather is set to continue in Hong Kong with maximum temperatures reaching 35 degrees Celsius. A Very Hot Weather Warning remains in effect due to weak winds and high temperatures across the city. However, meteorologists expect a low-pressure system to arrive by midweek, bringing squally thunderstorms and more unsettled weather conditions.

articles.title: Qatar Denies Detaining Iranian Pilots
articles.summary: Qatar has dismissed claims that it is holding Iranian pilots as misleading. Qatari officials stated that two Iranian bombers were intercepted after violating Qatari airspace earlier in the conflict. According to Doha, search-and-rescue teams later located the remains of the pilots, and diplomatic channels were used to coordinate matters in line with international humanitarian law.

articles.title: 1980s Knitwear Designer Rediscovers Lost Work
articles.summary: Liz Newman, a prominent knitwear designer from the 1980s who created garments worn by notable public figures such as Princess Diana and Olivia Newton-John, has seen her original patterns and designs brought back into public display at a gallery exhibition after previously believing they were entirely lost.

articles.title: Gangtok Recognized as Walkable City
articles.summary: Gangtok is highlighted as one of India's most walkable cities, where daily commutes, school runs, and social visits are predominantly conducted on foot. The city's pedestrian-friendly infrastructure offers an alternative model for urban planning compared to heavily vehicle-congested metropolitan areas.

articles.title: Mohamed Salah Makes Debut in Trabzonspor Draw
articles.summary: Mohamed Salah made his debut for Trabzonspor as a second-half substitute during a 1-1 draw against Kasimpasa in the Turkish Super Lig. Despite creating several scoring opportunities after coming on in the 58th minute, Trabzonspor failed to secure a victory, leaving the team's coach to call for significant improvements ahead of upcoming European fixtures.

articles.title: Political and Bureaucratic Turf Wars
articles.summary: Tensions and turf wars between political figures and government bureaucrats in Tokyo continue to be a notable dynamic. Observers note that this ongoing friction between elected officials and administrative structures is a long-standing issue rather than a recent development.

articles.title: Western Australian Schools Face Surge in Lockdowns
articles.summary: Parliamentary figures show that public schools in Western Australia were forced into lockdown 1,300 times over the past year. The majority of these security incidents were triggered by violent threats directed at students or staff members, highlighting growing safety concerns within educational institutions.

articles.title: Punjab Cashless Healthcare Scheme Reaches Milestone
articles.summary: Punjab's Mukh Mantri Sehat Yojana cashless healthcare scheme has surpassed six lakh treatments, according to Dr. Balbir Singh. The government initiative assists families across the region by covering a wide range of essential medical procedures, spanning from routine dialysis to advanced cancer care, significantly easing financial burdens.

articles.title: Hong Kong Craft Hub Faces Uncertain Future
articles.summary: Traditional handicraft shops in Hong Kong's Sham Shui Po neighbourhood are facing an uncertain future as veteran artisans and long-standing businesses close down. The area, historically known for textile and bead manufacturing, is seeing its manufacturing legacy fade as younger generations move away from the traditional trade.

articles.title: Severe Drought Exposes Historical Landmarks on the Danube
articles.summary: Record-low water levels along the Danube River have caused severe disruptions, including the complete emergence of the historical Rock of Starvation in Budapest. The ongoing drought has severely impacted local agriculture, drinking water supplies, and forced the temporary closure of several nuclear reactors due to insufficient cooling water.

articles.title: Cambodian Worker Exodus Highlights Thailand Labour Vulnerabilities
articles.summary: The departure of hundreds of thousands of migrant workers following border tensions with Cambodia has exposed vulnerabilities in Thailand's economic reliance on cross-border labor. While authorities have attempted to retain existing workers, international labor organizations warn that the heavy reliance on low-cost regional labor presents structural economic risks.

articles.title: Chinese Scientists Develop Electric Eel-Inspired Sensor for Robots
articles.summary: Researchers at Xidian University have developed a sensor that mimics the electric field radar used by electric eels. The technology enables robotic systems to detect and differentiate the material composition and surface conditions of approaching objects without making physical contact.

articles.title: Nandan Nilekani Leads Task Force to Overhaul Indian Exam System
articles.summary: Nandan Nilekani is heading a high-level task force tasked with reforming India's examination system following widespread paper leaks and subsequent national protests. The security breaches compromised major entrance exams, leading to significant political fallout and highlighting vulnerabilities in the distribution of official test materials.

articles.title: North Korean Leader Expresses Pride in Ties with Russia
articles.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un informed Russian President Vladimir Putin that he is proud of the strong bilateral relations between their two countries. According to state media reports, the statement highlights the ongoing diplomatic and strategic alignment between Pyongyang and Moscow.

articles.title: Rescue Teams Search for Survivors After Indonesian Earthquake
articles.summary: Rescue crews in eastern Indonesia are searching through collapsed buildings and landslide debris following a magnitude 7.7 earthquake. The disaster has resulted in at least 47 fatalities, more than 100 injuries, and thousands of displaced residents across multiple regencies on Flores Island.

articles.title: Newcastle Knights Host Gold Coast Titans in NRL Match
articles.summary: The Newcastle Knights are hosting the Gold Coast Titans in an NRL fixture as the team seeks to secure a position within the top four of the league standings. Fans and analysts are closely following the encounter as part of Sunday's rugby league schedule.

articles.title: Talgo Trains Schedule on Railway Lines
articles.summary: Spanish Talgo trains are among the fastest and newest operating on the railway authority network. They provide high levels of comfort and a quiet environment for passengers traveling across the various scheduled routes on the national railway system.

articles.title: New York Nuns Prioritize Immigrant Advocacy Before Closure
articles.summary: The Sisters of Charity in New York have announced that advocating for vulnerable immigrants and their children will be a primary focus of their final mission before the religious order concludes its operations.

articles.title: CBI Re-registers BSP Leader Armstrong Murder Case
articles.summary: Investigative authorities have officially re-registered the murder case of Bahujan Samaj Party leader Armstrong. As part of the ongoing investigation into the high-profile killing, officials visited the specific crime scene located in the Perambur area to gather further evidence.

articles.title: Giants and Blues Battle for AFL Wildcard
articles.summary: The Greater Western Sydney Giants and Carlton Blues face off in crucial matches that could determine the final composition of the top ten ladder. These games are pivotal in shaping the wildcard positions, with outcomes closely followed by supporters and analysts alike.

articles.title: Kate Douglass Breaks 50m Freestyle World Record
articles.summary: American swimmer Kate Douglass broke the women's 50m freestyle world record twice in a single day at the Pan Pacific Championships. She first clocked 23.49 seconds in the morning heats before lowering it to 23.19 seconds to win the final, surpassing the previous mark held by teammate Gretchen Walsh.

articles.title: Wheatfall and Ford Lead Tiger-Cats Victory
articles.summary: Keric Wheatfall and teammate Ford delivered standout performances to help the Tiger-Cats secure a victory over the Roughriders on Saturday night. The players executed key plays throughout the match, contributing significantly to the team's successful offensive strategy and final win.

articles.title: Guangdong Seeks to Retain and Attract AI Talent
articles.summary: China's Guangdong province is actively working to attract top computer science students from Tsinghua University to address a shortage of artificial intelligence talent. Despite producing prominent AI founders, the region previously struggled to retain them, prompting new initiatives to secure future industry leaders.

articles.title: Belgium Battles Largest Wildfire on Record
articles.summary: A rapidly spreading wildfire in the High Fens nature reserve near the German border has burned approximately 2,700 hectares. The blaze, the largest on record for the region, has prompted authorities to evacuate hundreds of residents from the affected areas as firefighters continue containment efforts.

articles.title: Wildfire Burns in Belgium Nature Reserve
articles.summary: A rapidly spreading wildfire in the High Fens nature reserve near the Belgian-German border has burned approximately 2,700 hectares. Authorities in the nearby German town of Monschau have warned residents that potential evacuation orders may be issued if the fire continues to advance.

articles.title: Egypt Ministry of Labour Announces Hotel Job Openings
articles.summary: Egypt's Ministry of Labour has announced 27 new job openings at a hotel, covering various hospitality and service specialisations. Monthly salaries range between 7,000 and 15,000 Egyptian pounds, depending on the specific position and the candidate's level of prior experience in the field.

articles.title: Death Toll Rises Following Powerful Earthquake in Colombia
articles.summary: Official estimates indicate that approximately 290 people have died following a powerful earthquake in Colombia. Rescue and recovery efforts are ongoing as authorities report roughly 140 people remain missing and nearly 4,000 individuals have sustained injuries from the natural disaster.

articles.title: North Korea and Russia Reaffirm Ties on Liberation Day
articles.summary: North Korea and Russia reaffirmed their bilateral ties on the anniversary of Korean Liberation Day. Relations between Pyongyang and Moscow have grown increasingly close following North Korea's deployment of military personnel and resources in support of Russia's ongoing military campaign in Ukraine.

articles.title: Japan Aims for the Moons of Mars
articles.summary: Japan is preparing to launch the unmanned MMX spacecraft from the Tanegashima Space Center in the coming months. The mission aims to explore the moons of Mars and could potentially lay essential groundwork for future human exploration efforts directed toward the red planet.

articles.title: Ebola Outbreak on Track to Be Worst in History
articles.summary: The World Health Organization reports that the ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is on track to become the worst in history. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus noted that numerous deaths are occurring outside known transmission chains, indicating the outbreak remains far from being brought under control.

articles.title: Chinese Man Connects Elderly Parents with Overseas Children
articles.summary: A former rural courier in central China has completed over 200 trips annually to remote mountain villages to visit elderly parents on behalf of their children living far away or overseas. Utilizing his deep knowledge of local winding roads from his delivery days, he helps bridge the geographical gap for isolated families.

articles.title: Global Sports Brands Expand Sponsorships Across the Gulf
articles.summary: Global sportswear brands are increasingly partnering with Gulf sports clubs, athletes, and events to expand their cultural influence and international reach. Recently, American brand New Balance signed a three-year deal with Abu Dhabi football club Al Jazira, joining a long line of international suppliers investing in the region.

articles.title: Ariana Grande Begins UK Tour Dates
articles.summary: Pop star Ariana Grande has arrived in the UK to perform the first of ten scheduled concert dates in London. Following the completion of these performances, the singer plans to temporarily step back from her public life.

articles.title: Australian Man Builds His Own Airplane
articles.summary: Central Queensland resident Len Neale has successfully built and flown his own aircraft, joining thousands of amateur aviation enthusiasts in Australia. The retired tradesman's project reflects a lifelong passion for aviation and fulfills a personal dream of constructing a custom-built plane.

articles.title: China Gang Crackdown Raises Wrongful Conviction Fears
articles.summary: Legal experts in China have expressed concern over potential wrongful convictions amid an ongoing crackdown on organized crime. The apprehension follows the severe sentencing of several business figures, including a real estate developer in Sichuan province who received a 20-year prison term after being classified as a gang leader.

articles.title: BTS Grammy Boycott Sparks Debate Over Asian Pop Recognition
articles.summary: The decision by South Korean group BTS not to submit their music for consideration at the upcoming Grammy Awards has reignited discussions about the representation of Asian artists. The move follows the introduction of a new best Asian pop music performance category, prompting debate among peers regarding industry recognition.

articles.title: Life in Dubai: Renting a Villanova Villa
articles.summary: A British expatriate living in Dubai shares his experience renting a four-bedroom villa in the Villanova community for 155,000 dirhams annually. Having lived in the UAE since 2007, he and his family have relocated multiple times across the city due to changing personal circumstances and rising rental prices in previous neighborhoods.

articles.title: Couple Balances Life, Love, and Work Together
articles.summary: Balancing personal and professional life often presents a challenge, but for Astrid Lorange and Andrew Brooks, love, life, and work are deeply intertwined. The couple navigates their relationship by serving as each other's biggest critics, which they credit for fueling their enduring personal and professional bond.

articles.title: Kerala Probes Failed Bid to Bring Messi to Kochi
articles.summary: The Kerala government is considering a multi-agency probe into the failed attempt to bring football star Lionel Messi to Kochi during the previous administration. Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan stated that a preliminary inquiry by the Sports Department uncovered very serious allegations regarding the matter.

articles.title: Minister Avoids Committing to NDIS Exit Delay
articles.summary: The Australian NDIS minister has declined to guarantee a delay in participant exits from the scheme even if necessary foundational supports are not fully ready. However, the minister insisted that the government remains committed to ensuring participants are adequately supported and will not be left without assistance.

articles.title: Former Nurse Shares Lessons from JAL Crash
articles.summary: Drawing from her experience responding to the aftermath of the 1985 Japan Airlines crash, a former nurse is sharing her knowledge of seitai. The traditional practice involves the careful physical arrangement of a deceased person's body to help provide closure for grieving families.

articles.title: Victoria Police to Recruit Retired Officers to Address Staffing Shortfall
articles.summary: Victoria Police plans to recruit hundreds of retired officers as reservists to alleviate the administrative burden on frontline personnel. The initiative aims to help bridge a staffing deficit of nearly 1,500 members within the police force.

articles.title: Qatar Denies Holding Missing Iranian Fighter Pilots
articles.summary: Qatar has officially denied claims by Tehran that Qatari forces captured three Iranian fighter pilots alive after their aircraft were shot down during the early days of the recent US-Israel conflict with Iran. Iran maintains that the pilots are being held by Qatari authorities.

articles.title: Australian Players Advance as Djokovic Exits Cincinnati Open
articles.summary: Australian tennis players Alex de Minaur and Rinky Hijikata have advanced at the Cincinnati Open following strong performances. Meanwhile, Novak Djokovic suffered an early exit from the tournament, marking a notable upset in the men's singles draw.

articles.title: Transport Technology Institute Opens Admissions
articles.summary: The Higher Institute for Transport Technology in Vardan, affiliated with the Ministry of Transport and supervised by the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research, has announced the opening of admission applications for a new academic batch for the years 2026 and 2027, welcoming eligible students to apply according to the established official guidelines and requirements.

articles.title: Daily Cairo-Alexandria Train Schedules
articles.summary: The railway authority has established fixed daily schedules for train operations on the Cairo and Alexandria route in both directions. Because many travelers rely on railway transportation, official timetables for various train classes are published regularly to help passengers plan their journeys efficiently across the national railway network.

articles.title: Canberra's Hands On Studio Celebrates 30th Anniversary
articles.summary: Canberra's Hands On Studio is celebrating its 30th anniversary, highlighted by artist Stephen Corsini, who has attended the studio for three decades. Corsini hopes his newly created portrait of Australia's first female prime minister will eventually be displayed in Parliament House.

articles.title: Explosions Reported in Kyiv
articles.summary: Several explosions were heard in the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv early Sunday morning. The sounds coincided with official warnings issued by local authorities regarding an incoming ballistic missile attack targeting the city, prompting air raid alerts and safety measures for residents across the metropolitan area.

articles.title: Australia vs Bangladesh First Test Day Four
articles.summary: Live updates from day four of the first men's Test match between Australia and Bangladesh at Marrara Cricket Ground in Darwin. Australia faced pressure as Alex Carey was dismissed early, while Cameron Green worked to build the score past fifty, leaving the team fighting to secure a meaningful position against Bangladesh's bowling attack.

articles.title: World War II Survivor Calls for Peace on Anniversary
articles.summary: Kazuhiko Takahashi, a 98-year-old survivor, marked the 81st anniversary of the end of World War II by urging the public to remember the millions of Japanese lives lost and pledging a continued commitment to global peace.

articles.title: Dodgers Optimistic About Ohtani's Mound Return
articles.summary: Los Angeles Dodgers player Shohei Ohtani completed his first bullpen session since July 22, when he was sidelined due to a throwing setback while on the road in Philadelphia. Team staff and management expressed optimism regarding his ongoing recovery and potential eventual return to pitching for the major league club.

articles.title: Chiba Downpour Death Toll Rises to Nine
articles.summary: The death toll following heavy downpours in Chiba has risen to nine people, with at least two victims discovered inside submerged vehicles. Local authorities report that nearly 500 residents have been evacuated from their homes as emergency response operations continue.

articles.title: Couple Recovers From Crash
articles.summary: Andy and Callie Rigby have embarked on one of their favorite day trips four years after surviving a severe head-on collision with a bus. The journey marks a significant milestone in their long road to physical and emotional recovery following the traumatic traffic accident that deeply impacted their daily lives.
